subject: Intermittent path failures to BrightWave private deployment — routing/NAT/MTU triage
messages:
From: Ingrid Hayes <ingrid.hayes@brightwave.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — sudden 502s / TLS resets

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

We started seeing intermittent 502s and TLS session resets to our private Redwood deployment this morning around 08:40 PDT. App logs show a sharp spike in connection failures for flows originating from our on-prem env (10.10.0.0/22) when payloads exceed ~1400 bytes. Short/simple requests succeed fine.

Symptoms: 
- Clients behind our Edge firewall receive TCP RST or TLS handshake timeouts after 1-2s.
- Logs on our LB show backend 502 or connection reset while upstream (Redwood) shows no obvious app errors.
- tcpdump attached (brightwave-trace-20260825.pcap) and a filtered trace (edge-tcptrace-20260825.txt).

We’re running a VPC peering + transit VNAT that Redwood helped set up earlier this year. Can you triage? This is affecting a small set of customers but impacts our internal QA.

Thanks,
Ingrid Hayes
SRE Lead, BrightWave Logistics
ops@brightwave.com

(attachment: brightwave-trace-20260825.pcap, edge-tcptrace-20260825.txt)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — sudden 502s / TLS resets

Thanks Ingrid — sorry you’re seeing this. We’ll treat as high priority.

Quick plan: 
1) I’ll loop in our networking lead (Rishi) to do packet-level triage and look at SNAT/return-paths.
2) Please confirm an upcoming 60-minute debug window today (PDT) when we can run targeted captures and test payloads ~1500–1600 bytes.
3) If possible share the VPC route tables (eg: outputs of `ip route`/`aws ec2 describe-route-tables`) and the exact client IPs we should target.

We’ll start with determining if packets > MTU are being dropped (PMTU/DF) or if there’s asymmetric SNAT causing return traffic to take a path that rewrites source and breaks session affinity.

I’ve attached a short triage checklist for the session.

- Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
(attachment: triage-checklist-brief.txt)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ingrid Hayes <ingrid.hayes@brightwave.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — sudden 502s / TLS resets

Looping in my initial read of the artifacts Ingrid attached. High-level observations (quick triage):

- The tcpdump (edge-tcptrace) shows client -> LB -> Redwood SYN/ACK, then client sends a PSH with ~1468 bytes payload and we see MTU fragmentation signs (DF bit set, subsequent ICMP frag-needed in some samples). A number of these fragments are not seen coming back from the Redwood side.

- More concerning: some sessions show the return traffic coming from a different NAT IP than we have recorded in the peering config. That implies one of two things: (a) there's an intermediate SNAT at the transit/firewall doing source translation on egress, or (b) some return path uses a different egress (asymmetric routing) where sessions are being SNATted and don't match conntrack on the client-facing firewall.

Commands I’d like run in your environment (if you can paste outputs):
- `sudo ip route show` on the BrightWave edge
- `sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v` (or equivalent on your firewall)
- Any BGP neighbor state and route-map that might rewrite next-hops

Quick mitigation options to validate during the debug window:
- Temporarily disable DF/enable fragmentation (not ideal) to confirm MTU hypothesis.
- Add an explicit SNAT-exemption on the transit firewall for the client CIDR -> Redwood CIDR so responses are not rewritten mid-path.
- If asymmetric path is confirmed, add a return-route through the same egress or pin the flow via policy-based routing.

I’ll stand by for captures during the window. Also opened an INF ticket to track the work: INF-4521.

— Rishi
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Thanks Rishi — that asymmetry + MTU combo would explain why larger payloads trigger client-side resets.

Operational / customer-facing plan:
- Request a debug window tomorrow 09:00–10:00 PDT (BrightWave confirmed availability below).
- During the window we will: run targeted `ping -M do -s 1472` tests, BPF captures on our edge and RD-side peering interface, and a temporary SNAT-exempt rule in the transit firewall (config diff attached) to validate behavior.
- If the SNAT exemption mitigates, we’ll coordinate a follow-up change to add a persistent policy and schedule a maintenance window to implement safely.

Rollback plan if a change causes regressions: remove the SNAT-exempt rule and restore previous ACLs within 15 minutes. We’ll keep the customer on a dedicated rollout path if needed.

I’ve attached a proposed config diff: config-diff-snatexempt.patch. Please review before the session.

— Marissa Cole

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Ingrid Hayes <ingrid.hayes@brightwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — sudden 502s / TLS resets

Great debug session today — thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Summary & next steps: 

Summary of findings:
- Confirmed PMTU/fragmentation events when payloads > ~1400 bytes (DF set caused frag-needed ICMPs).
- Confirmed asymmetric return path: transit firewall was performing SNAT for a subset of egress routes which caused replies to come from a different NAT IP and break conntrack on the client-side firewall.

Immediate mitigations we tested: 
- Temporary SNAT exemption (applied and validated) for BrightWave CIDR -> Redwood CIDR eliminated the 502s for large payloads during the window.
- As a short-term workaround we also validated application-level throughput lowering (MSS clamp to 1400) as a fallback but that is not ideal long-term.

Planned permanent work: 
1) INF-4521: Implement policy-based routing on BrightWave transit to ensure symmetric egress/ingress path for client flows (owner: BrightWave network team).
2) Redwood action: we will add a monitoring alert to detect SNAT IP drift on peering connections and include a pinned fallback route to force symmetric return through the expected NAT pool (owner: Rishi).
3) Schedule a maintenance window to deploy the persistent SNAT-exempt rule and validate at scale (target: Aug 31, 22:00 PDT).

Rollback: removing the SNAT-exempt rule will restore previous behavior; we will keep canary traffic and have immediate rollback playbook in the ticket.

Open artifacts: config-diff-snatexempt.patch, brightwave-trace-20260825.pcap, edge-tcptrace-20260825.txt uploaded to INF-4521.

If BrightWave confirms the transit changes and the Aug 31 window works, we’ll close this ticket.

Thanks again — nice cross-team work.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
